items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And my first teacher was Rag Baby Stevens.

ctx.x: August the 15th, 1903. My father was a bass drummer in one of the early jazz bands of New Orleans. It was called Fish's Ragtime Military Jazz Band. And my first teacher was Rag Baby Stevens. And my first job was in the carnival parade. In those days the only parade that had any jazz in it at all was the Rex parade, which was a union. The only union parade of all the parades.
How many of those bands would really swing there in the Rex parade?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: And he, we worked some little things up between us, between he and I and my dad.

ctx.x: And you carried a bass drum. No, a snare drum. A snare drum.

We used two snare drums. And another thing that we did, that they did in Fisher's band, like when the band was stopped and wasn't playing, most of the other bands would just play brr-r-rump, brr-r-rump, brr-r-rump, brr-rump, brr-rump, you see. Well, this rag bear, that's why they call him rag bear. And he, we worked some little things up between us, between he and I and my dad. And we brr-rump, brr-rump, you jazz like, you know, licks, like the kids do now in the high school and the college bands, you know.
Was that the first time, to your knowledge, that anybody had made those renovations?
